title: Pinning contract: hybrid selectors, stability windows, and client-side safety checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define an unambiguous, backwards-compatible pin-resolution contract for the Redwood API/SDK that supports three selector classes (mutable tags, semver ranges, immutable commit hashes), exposes runtime fallback behavior, and surfaces client-side safety signals to prevent accidental instability. This ticket covers the API surface, SDK ergonomics, server-side resolution precedence, audit events, and ties to model performance profiles published during onboarding.
background: We currently allow multiple ways to reference models (tags, aliases, release channels). Customers pin to avoid silent changes, but ambiguity in resolution and implicit fallbacks have caused incidents where a model changed under a tag during a rollout. There is also a need for workloads to express 'prefer a variant with this performance profile' when multiple compatible versions exist.
proposed_api_spec:
Resolution selectors: 
- exact: model@sha256:<digest> (immutable)
- semver: model~^1.2.0 or model~>=1.2.3 <2.0.0 (best effort match)
- tag: model:stable or model:latest (mutable)

Behavior: 
1) If selector is exact (sha) -> resolve to exact artifact; fail if not present.
2) If selector is semver -> resolve to highest published version satisfying range; if no match, follow fallback rules.
3) If selector is tag -> resolve to the tag's current mapping at resolution time; warn if tag points to a mutable alias updated within a stability window.

Fallback rules (configurable per-request): 
- fail (default for critical workloads)
- fallback_to_compatible: try other versions with compatible model architecture and same perf-profile family
- runtime_degraded: route to lower-cost variant if requested but mark response.metadata.fallback = true

Perf profile hinting: selectors may include a performance preference suffix, e.g. model~^1.0.0?profile=latency-1 or model@sha256:<digest>?profile=cost-quantized. The runtime will prefer matches with that published performance tag.

Audit & tracing: resolution steps, chosen artifact id, and perf profile used MUST be emitted to audit logs and returned in response.headers.X-Model-Resolution.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API accepts selectors in three classes and persists resolution metadata.
2) Runtime implements precedence rules and configurable fallback per request.
3) SDKs surface easy-to-use constructors and emit client-side validation warnings when using mutable tags.
4) Audit log includes resolved artifact id and perf profile id for every inference.
5) Documentation and migration guide published.
6) Automated tests cover semantic permutations and failure modes.
tests: Unit: selector parser handles tag/semver/sha paths and rejects malformed refs
Integration: server resolves semver ranges across multiple onboarded versions and honors perf profile preference
E2E: request with fallback_to_compatible returns marked response and audit entry when exact version missing
Chaos: simulate tag repointing during in-flight requests to validate client warning semantics
migration_plan:
Phase 1 (non-breaking): accept selector variants and default to current behavior (fail on unresolvable). Emit deprecation warnings for usages where clients pin to mutable tags without explicit stability window.
Phase 2: enable per-request fallback flags and perf-profile preference.
Phase 3: default SDKs will make tag->mutable mapping explicit and recommend semver or commit pins for production. Provide a CLI tool to scan org usage and flag mutable tags in workloads.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind 'pin-contract-v1' for hosted and dedicated control planes.
2) Enable read-only resolution and additional headers for 2 weeks to collect telemetry.
3) Offer opt-in period for customers to test fallback behaviors.
4) Gradual enforcement with migration window (60 days) before making fail-on-missing the default for critical SLAs.
notes: Trade-offs: Enforcing strict immutability increases operational friction for users iterating on models; semver gives balance but requires model publishers to adopt semver ordering discipline.
Decision: prefer explicitness — SDKs will emit warnings for tag use in production and provide helpers to convert tags to hashes (resolve-and-pin).
Open question: how to express compatibility semantics across model forks (e.g., quantized vs fp16). Proposal: publisher-provided compatibility labels during onboarding (compat:semantic-id).
